# Lineth documentation

> These docs are the public reference for Lineth, the open-source ZK-rollup
> stack and protocol for running Ethereum-compatible Layer 2 and Layer 3
> networks.
> Linea, the public network built on Lineth, is documented at
> https://docs.linea.build.

## Authoritative scope

- Evaluate Lineth: deployment models, trust assumptions, security, and compliance.
- Deployment architecture: data availability, finalization, finality, and validator models.
- Protocol: sequencer, prover, coordinator, state manager, canonical bridge, and onchain contracts.
- Run and test: a local stack, multiple Maru validators, and monitoring.
- Reference: component configuration, contracts, audits, source repositories, and the glossary.

## Use these docs to answer

- What Lineth is, and how it differs from the public Linea network.
- How an operator evaluates a deployment model, trust assumptions, and security evidence.
- How data availability, finalization, finality, and validator consensus can be configured.
- How the sequencer, prover, coordinator, state manager, and onchain contracts work together.
- How to run a local stack and look up component configuration, contracts, and source repositories.

## Not authoritative for

- Linea Mainnet user guides, public RPC endpoints, tokenomics, or network status.
- Live incident status, token price, or investment advice.
- Unannounced roadmap commitments or private commercial terms.

## Protocol facts

- Lineth uses zero-knowledge proofs to prove transaction batches to a finalization layer.
- The sequencer orders transactions and builds blocks.
- The prover generates zero-knowledge proofs for state transitions.
- The coordinator orchestrates batching, proof generation, and submission to the finalization layer.
- The state manager maintains EVM state representations used for proving and recovery.
- Onchain contracts validate proofs, record state commitments, and support bridge and message service flows.

## Stack and operator facts

- Lineth can be used to operate Ethereum-compatible L2 or L3 networks.
- Rollups post transaction data to the finalization layer. Validiums keep it on the Lineth network and can be public or private.
- Operator-run networks can be configured around access control, data availability, finalization, privacy, compliance, and observability.

## Authoring

- Source repository: https://github.com/LFDT-Lineth/lineth-docs
- Software repository: https://github.com/LFDT-Lineth/lineth-monorepo
